roles.label: First line
roles.responsibility: Owns and manages the risk it generates. Business units, risk owners and (for liquidity) Treasury identify, measure, mitigate and report their own risks, put controls in place, and escalate weaknesses to the second line.
examples: Identifies operational risks and establishes controls (ORR-2)
Tests the key controls it uses every day (ORR-5)
Treasury owns the liquidity stress test model (LTR-9)
Trains staff to report suspicious transactions (ORR-10)

roles.label: Second line
roles.responsibility: Oversees the first line independently. Risk management, compliance and legal (including the CRO's office and the AML/CFT officer) set policies and procedures, challenge Line 1's measurement and reporting, and aggregate risk data.
examples: Acts as AML/CFT contact person, with no business-line duties (ORR-10)
Advises on credit rather than approving it (CR-2)

roles.label: Third line
roles.responsibility: Gives independent assurance. Internal audit (and external auditors) review controls and adherence to policy, stay strictly separate from other departments, and report to internal and external stakeholders.
examples: Reviews controls and adherence to policies (ORR-2)
Usually tests controls; ORM only receives the results (ORR-5)
Periodically reviews the liquidity stress testing framework (LTR-9)

roles.label: Board / committee
roles.responsibility: Sets direction and oversees from above the three lines. The board and its risk and audit committees, plus governing committees with delegated oversight (ALCO, credit committee), set tolerance, approve frameworks, plans and exceptions, and monitor senior management.
examples: Sets operational risk tolerance and approves the ORMF (ORR-2)
Approves the capital plan management presents (ORR-20)
Approves credit guidelines sponsored by the CFO or CRO (CR-2)
ALCO holds overall responsibility for liquidity stress testing (LTR-9)
Audit committee receives internal audit reports on controls (ORR-6)
